subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOL0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOL0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
